category: Neural Networks II: Additional Layers, Net Surgery, Encoders/Decoders & NetTrain Options
description: The neural-network layers not covered in the basic chunk (shape and sequence layers, normalization variants, function/constant layers, aggregation, extra losses, random and placeholder layers, spatial transformers, augmentation) and the operators that combine them; plus functions that edit and inspect nets, the NetEncoder/NetDecoder types, shared arrays and stateful evaluation, and the NetTrain options for batches, learning rates, losses, validation, stopping, checkpointing, devices and reporting.

tools.name: FlattenLayer
tools.description: Flattens an input array into a vector (or flattens only the first n dimensions), the standard bridge from convolutional feature maps to LinearLayer; ReshapeLayer (listed) is the general reshaping form and TransposeLayer permutes dimensions (e.g. to swap channel and sequence axes). These shape layers have no parameters and infer sizes automatically inside NetChain.
tools.usage:
FlattenLayer[]
FlattenLayer[n]
FlattenLayer[-1]
TransposeLayer[]
TransposeLayer[{1 <-> 2}]
TransposeLayer[{3, 1, 2}]

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of leading dimensions to flatten (negative counts from the end).

tools.example:
NetChain[{ConvolutionLayer[16, 3], Ramp, PoolingLayer[2], FlattenLayer[], LinearLayer[10], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Image", {28, 28}, "Grayscale"}], "Output" -> NetDecoder[{"Class", Range[0, 9]}]]
TransposeLayer[{1 <-> 2}][RandomReal[1, {3, 5}]] // Dimensions (* {5, 3} *)

tools.name: PaddingLayer
tools.description: Pads an array with zeros, a fixed value, or by "Reflected"/"Fixed" extension on each side of each dimension - used for "same" convolutions, sequence alignment and making sizes match before CatenateLayer; PartLayer extracts a part (slice) of an array with Span specifications and ExtractLayer extracts elements at a position supplied as a second input (e.g. picking the vector at a given time step).
tools.usage:
PaddingLayer[{{n1, n2}, {m1, m2}}]
PaddingLayer[{{1, 1}, {1, 1}}, "Padding" -> 0.]
PaddingLayer[{{0, 0}, {2, 2}}, "Padding" -> "Reflected"]
PartLayer[spec]
PartLayer[2 ;; 5]
PartLayer[{All, 1}]
ExtractLayer[]

parameters.name: {{n1, n2}, ...}
parameters.description: Padding amounts before/after for each dimension.

tools.example:
NetChain[{PaddingLayer[{{0, 0}, {1, 1}, {1, 1}}], ConvolutionLayer[8, 3]}, "Input" -> {3, 32, 32}] (* keeps 32x32 *)
PartLayer[-1][{{1, 2}, {3, 4}, {5, 6}}] (* {5, 6}: last time step *)

tools.name: ReplicateLayer
tools.description: Replicates an array n times along a new (or specified) dimension - broadcasting a vector to every time step or every pixel so it can be catenated with a sequence or image; AppendLayer / PrependLayer add an element to a sequence, and SequenceReverseLayer, SequenceLastLayer, SequenceMostLayer, SequenceRestLayer and SequenceIndicesLayer are the sequence-editing layers used in encoder-decoder and attention models.
tools.usage:
ReplicateLayer[n]
ReplicateLayer[n, level]
ReplicateLayer[Automatic] (* match a sequence length *)
AppendLayer[]
PrependLayer[]
SequenceReverseLayer[]
SequenceLastLayer[]
SequenceMostLayer[]
SequenceRestLayer[]
SequenceIndicesLayer[]

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of copies, or Automatic to infer from another input.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Dimension at which to insert the copies.

tools.example:
ReplicateLayer[3][{1, 2}] (* {{1,2},{1,2},{1,2}} *)
NetGraph[<|"emb" -> EmbeddingLayer[16], "rev" -> SequenceReverseLayer[], "last" -> SequenceLastLayer[], "cls" -> LinearLayer[2], "sm" -> SoftmaxLayer[]|>, {"emb" -> "rev" -> "last" -> "cls" -> "sm"}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Tokens"}]]

tools.name: AggregationLayer
tools.description: Aggregates an array over specified levels with Mean, Total, Max, Min or StandardDeviation (e.g. global average pooling over spatial dimensions, or mean over a sequence); SummationLayer sums over all dimensions to a scalar, TotalLayer sums several equally shaped inputs elementwise and DotLayer computes dot products (or batched matrix products) of two inputs. These parameter-free reductions are the building blocks of attention scores and pooling heads.
tools.usage:
AggregationLayer[Mean]
AggregationLayer[Max, 1]
AggregationLayer[Mean, {2, 3}] (* global average pooling over H, W *)
SummationLayer[]
TotalLayer[]
DotLayer[]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Mean, Total, Max, Min, StandardDeviation, Variance.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Dimension(s) aggregated (default All but the first).

tools.example:
NetChain[{ConvolutionLayer[64, 3], Ramp, AggregationLayer[Mean, {2, 3}], LinearLayer[10], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> {3, 32, 32}]
NetGraph[{DotLayer[], SoftmaxLayer[]}, {{NetPort["q"], NetPort["k"]} -> 1 -> 2}]

tools.name: NormalizationLayer
tools.description: Normalizes activations over specified levels with learnable scale and bias - configurable as layer norm, instance norm or group norm depending on the aggregation levels and "GroupNumber" - as used in transformers and style-transfer networks; InstanceNormalizationLayer and LocalResponseNormalizationLayer are the specialised forms, and BatchNormalizationLayer (listed) normalizes over the batch. Choose NormalizationLayer for sequence models and small batches.
tools.usage:
NormalizationLayer[]
NormalizationLayer[levels]
NormalizationLayer[{2, 3}] (* instance norm for {C, H, W} *)
NormalizationLayer[All, "Epsilon" -> 10^-5]
InstanceNormalizationLayer[]
LocalResponseNormalizationLayer[r]

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Levels over which statistics are computed (default all).

tools.example:
block = NetChain[{LinearLayer[256], NormalizationLayer[], ElementwiseLayer["GELU"], LinearLayer[256]}];
NetChain[{ConvolutionLayer[32, 3], InstanceNormalizationLayer[], Ramp}, "Input" -> {3, 64, 64}]

tools.name: FunctionLayer
tools.description: Wraps an arbitrary Wolfram Language function of arrays (using Map, Dot, Ramp, Sin, Table, Part, etc.) as a differentiable net layer, compiled automatically for training - the escape hatch for custom operations without writing a dedicated layer; CompiledLayer wraps compiled code (FunctionCompile-style typed functions) for maximum speed and ConstantArrayLayer / ConstantPlusLayer / ConstantTimesLayer inject learnable or fixed constants.
tools.usage:
FunctionLayer[f]
FunctionLayer[#^2 + 1 &]
FunctionLayer[Function[{x, y}, x*y + Sin[y]]]
FunctionLayer[f, "Input" -> {3}]
CompiledLayer[cf]
ConstantArrayLayer["Array" -> arr]
ConstantArrayLayer[{n}] (* learnable *)
ConstantPlusLayer["Biases" -> {1, 2, 3}]
ConstantTimesLayer["Scaling" -> 2]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Pure function of one or several array arguments; multi-argument functions create several input ports.

tools.notes: FunctionLayer introduced in 12.2; functions must be expressible in the compilable subset used by the net framework.

tools.name: ParametricRampLayer
tools.description: PReLU: a rectified-linear layer whose negative slope is a learnable parameter (per channel or shared), often improving over Ramp in deep CNNs; ElementwiseLayer (listed) provides the fixed activations ("ReLU", "GELU", "ELU", "SELU", "Swish", Tanh, LogisticSigmoid, "SoftSign", ...). Use ParametricRampLayer when the activation slope should adapt during training.
tools.usage:
ParametricRampLayer[]
ParametricRampLayer["Slope" -> 0.1]
ParametricRampLayer["Slope" -> Automatic, "Input" -> {16, 8, 8}]
ElementwiseLayer["GELU"]
ElementwiseLayer["SELU"]
tools.example: NetChain[{ConvolutionLayer[32, 3], ParametricRampLayer[], PoolingLayer[2], FlattenLayer[], LinearLayer[10], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Image", 32, "RGB"}]]

tools.name: DeconvolutionLayer
tools.description: Transposed convolution (upsampling) layer with n output channels and given kernel size, stride and padding - the decoder counterpart of ConvolutionLayer used in autoencoders, U-Nets, segmentation and GAN generators; ResizeLayer instead resizes spatial dimensions by interpolation ("Nearest", "Linear") without learnable parameters. Supports 1D, 2D and 3D data.
tools.usage:
DeconvolutionLayer[n, s]
DeconvolutionLayer[n, {h, w}, "Stride" -> 2, "PaddingSize" -> 1]
ResizeLayer[{h, w}]
ResizeLayer[{Scaled[2], Scaled[2]}]
ResizeLayer[{h, w}, "Resampling" -> "Nearest"]
tools.example:
decoder = NetChain[{LinearLayer[128*4*4], ReshapeLayer[{128, 4, 4}], DeconvolutionLayer[64, 4, "Stride" -> 2, "PaddingSize" -> 1], Ramp, DeconvolutionLayer[1, 4, "Stride" -> 2, "PaddingSize" -> 1], LogisticSigmoid}, "Input" -> 32]
NetChain[{ResizeLayer[{Scaled[2], Scaled[2]}], ConvolutionLayer[16, 3, "PaddingSize" -> 1]}]

tools.name: SpatialTransformationLayer
tools.description: Applies an affine transformation (given as a second input of 6 parameters, typically predicted by a small localization net) to an image-like input and resamples it to a given output size - the spatial transformer module that lets networks learn to crop, rotate and rescale their input for invariance.
tools.usage:
SpatialTransformationLayer[{h, w}]
SpatialTransformationLayer[{h, w}, "Input" -> {c, hin, win}]
tools.example:
loc = NetChain[{FlattenLayer[], LinearLayer[32], Ramp, LinearLayer[6]}];
stn = NetGraph[<|"loc" -> loc, "st" -> SpatialTransformationLayer[{28, 28}]|>, {NetPort["Input"] -> "loc", {NetPort["Input"], "loc"} -> "st"}, "Input" -> {1, 40, 40}]

tools.name: ImageAugmentationLayer
tools.description: Performs random cropping (to a given size) and optional horizontal/vertical reflection of image inputs during training only (identity at evaluation), a built-in data-augmentation layer that improves generalisation of image classifiers without preprocessing the dataset. Place it right after the image encoder.
tools.usage:
ImageAugmentationLayer[{h, w}]
ImageAugmentationLayer[{h, w}, "ReflectionProbabilities" -> {0.5, 0}]
ImageAugmentationLayer[{h, w}, "Input" -> {3, hin, win}]
tools.example: net = NetChain[{ImageAugmentationLayer[{28, 28}, "ReflectionProbabilities" -> {0.5, 0}], ConvolutionLayer[32, 3], Ramp, PoolingLayer[2], FlattenLayer[], LinearLayer[10], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Image", {32, 32}, "Grayscale"}]]

tools.name: OrderingLayer
tools.description: Sorts or gives the ordering of the elements of its input (ascending/descending, optionally the top-k), enabling differentiable-friendly ranking heads and k-max pooling; UnitVectorLayer converts integer class indices into one-hot vectors (the inverse of a Class decoder) for use inside NetGraph, e.g. in sequence-to-sequence teacher forcing.
tools.usage:
OrderingLayer[]
OrderingLayer[k]
OrderingLayer[k, "Descending"]
UnitVectorLayer[n]
UnitVectorLayer[n, "Input" -> "Integer"]

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of leading positions to return.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Length of the unit vectors (number of classes).

tools.example:
OrderingLayer[3, "Descending"][{0.1, 0.7, 0.2, 0.9}] (* {4, 2, 3} *)
UnitVectorLayer[5][3] (* {0, 0, 1, 0, 0} *)

tools.name: MeanAbsoluteLossLayer
tools.description: L1 loss between input and target arrays (robust regression), complementing MeanSquaredLossLayer and CrossEntropyLossLayer (listed); ContrastiveLossLayer implements the Siamese-network contrastive loss on pairs with a margin, and CTCLossLayer the connectionist temporal classification loss for unaligned sequence labelling (speech, OCR). Loss layers are attached via the LossFunction option of NetTrain or inside a NetGraph with a "Loss" port.
tools.usage:
MeanAbsoluteLossLayer[]
ContrastiveLossLayer[]
ContrastiveLossLayer["Margin" -> 1.]
CTCLossLayer[]
CTCLossLayer["Target" -> NetEncoder[{"Characters", chars}]]
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> MeanAbsoluteLossLayer[]]

parameters.name: Margin
parameters.description: Margin for dissimilar pairs in the contrastive loss.

tools.example:
NetTrain[NetChain[{LinearLayer[32], Ramp, LinearLayer[1]}], data, LossFunction -> MeanAbsoluteLossLayer[]]
ocr = NetGraph[<|"conv" -> ..., "gru" -> GatedRecurrentLayer[128], "cls" -> NetMapOperator[LinearLayer[27]], "sm" -> SoftmaxLayer[], "ctc" -> CTCLossLayer["Target" -> NetEncoder[{"Characters", Alphabet[]}]]|>, {"conv" -> "gru" -> "cls" -> "sm" -> "ctc", NetPort["Target"] -> "ctc"}]

tools.name: RandomArrayLayer
tools.description: A layer with no input that emits a random array drawn from a distribution (Normal, Uniform, Bernoulli, ...) each time the net is evaluated in training mode - the noise source for variational autoencoders (reparameterization), GAN generators and dropout-like regularization; PlaceholderLayer marks a position in a net whose operation is not yet defined (for incremental net construction) and cannot be evaluated until replaced.
tools.usage:
RandomArrayLayer[NormalDistribution[], "Output" -> {n}]
RandomArrayLayer[UniformDistribution[{-1, 1}], "Output" -> {100}]
RandomArrayLayer[BernoulliDistribution[0.5], "Output" -> {8, 8}]
PlaceholderLayer[]
PlaceholderLayer["tag"]
NetReplacePart[net, "placeholder" -> LinearLayer[10]]
tools.example: vae = NetGraph[<|"mean" -> LinearLayer[2], "logvar" -> LinearLayer[2], "noise" -> RandomArrayLayer[NormalDistribution[], "Output" -> {2}], "std" -> ElementwiseLayer[Exp[#/2] &], "scale" -> ThreadingLayer[Times], "z" -> ThreadingLayer[Plus]|>, {NetPort["Input"] -> "mean", NetPort["Input"] -> "logvar" -> "std", {"std", "noise"} -> "scale", {"mean", "scale"} -> "z"}, "Input" -> 32]

tools.name: BasicRecurrentLayer
tools.description: The simple (Elman) recurrent layer h_t = Tanh[W x_t + U h_{t-1} + b] with n hidden units, the lightweight alternative to LongShortTermMemoryLayer and GatedRecurrentLayer (listed) for short sequences; all recurrent layers accept variable-length sequence inputs, expose "State" ports and can be run in bidirectional form with NetBidirectionalOperator.
tools.usage:
BasicRecurrentLayer[n]
BasicRecurrentLayer[n, "Dropout" -> 0.2]
BasicRecurrentLayer[n, "Input" -> {"Varying", d}]

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of hidden units (output size per step).

tools.example: NetChain[{EmbeddingLayer[16], BasicRecurrentLayer[32], SequenceLastLayer[], LinearLayer[2], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Tokens"}], "Output" -> NetDecoder[{"Class", {"neg", "pos"}}]]

tools.name: NetBidirectionalOperator
tools.description: Runs a recurrent layer (or two different ones) forward and backward over a sequence and combines the outputs (catenation by default, or Plus/Mean), giving bidirectional RNNs for tagging, speech and text classification; NetNestOperator applies a net n times in sequence (weight-shared deep nets, iterative refinement) and NetMapThreadOperator maps a net over several sequences in parallel (the multi-input form of NetMapOperator).
tools.usage:
NetBidirectionalOperator[LongShortTermMemoryLayer[64]]
NetBidirectionalOperator[{fwdLayer, bwdLayer}]
NetBidirectionalOperator[layer, "Aggregation" -> Mean]
NetNestOperator[net, n]
NetMapThreadOperator[net]
tools.example:
tagger = NetChain[{EmbeddingLayer[64], NetBidirectionalOperator[GatedRecurrentLayer[64]], NetMapOperator[LinearLayer[9]], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Tokens"}], "Output" -> NetDecoder[{"Class", tags}]]
NetNestOperator[NetChain[{LinearLayer[16], Tanh}], 4]

tools.name: NetGANOperator
tools.description: Combines a generator net and a discriminator (classification) net into a single trainable object implementing generative adversarial training with the standard loss (or "Wasserstein" and other loss types); NetTrain then alternates updates automatically and the trained generator is extracted with NetExtract. NetPairEmbeddingOperator similarly wraps a net for Siamese pair-embedding training with ContrastiveLossLayer.
tools.usage:
gan = NetGANOperator[{generator, discriminator}]
gan = NetGANOperator[{generator, discriminator}, "Wasserstein"]
trained = NetTrain[gan, <|"Sample" -> realData, "Latent" -> RandomVariate[NormalDistribution[], {n, d}]|>]
NetExtract[trained, "Generator"]
NetPairEmbeddingOperator[net]

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description: Net mapping latent vectors to samples.

parameters.name: discriminator
parameters.description: Net mapping samples to a real/fake score.

tools.name: Transformer encoder block
tools.description: Idiom for a transformer encoder block built from listed layers: AttentionLayer (multi-head self-attention), ThreadingLayer[Plus] residual connections, NormalizationLayer (layer norm) and a position-wise feed-forward NetMapOperator; NetArrayLayer supplies learned positional embeddings or class tokens (broadcast with ReplicateLayer). Stack blocks with NetNestOperator or NetChain and feed token sequences from a "SubwordTokens" or "Tokens" encoder.
tools.usage:
NetArrayLayer["Output" -> {n, d}]
NetGraph[<|"pos" -> NetArrayLayer["Output" -> {32, 64}], "add" -> ThreadingLayer[Plus]|>, {{NetPort["Input"], "pos"} -> "add"}]
tools.example:
encoderBlock = NetGraph[<|"attn" -> AttentionLayer["Dot", "MultiHead" -> True, "Dimensions" -> 8], "add1" -> ThreadingLayer[Plus], "norm1" -> NormalizationLayer[], "ff" -> NetMapOperator[NetChain[{LinearLayer[256], ElementwiseLayer["GELU"], LinearLayer[64]}]], "add2" -> ThreadingLayer[Plus], "norm2" -> NormalizationLayer[]|>,
  {NetPort["Input"] -> NetPort["attn", "Query"], NetPort["Input"] -> NetPort["attn", "Key"], NetPort["Input"] -> NetPort["attn", "Value"], {NetPort["Input"], "attn"} -> "add1" -> "norm1", "norm1" -> "ff", {"norm1", "ff"} -> "add2" -> "norm2"}, "Input" -> {"Varying", 64}]

tools.name: ConvolutionLayer options
tools.description: ConvolutionLayer and PoolingLayer (listed) take the options that define modern CNN blocks: "Stride", "PaddingSize" (integer, per-side lists or "Same"), "Dilation", "ChannelGroups" (grouped/depthwise convolutions), "Interleaving" (channels-last input), "Function" (Max/Mean pooling), and "Input"/"Output" shape hints; 1D and 3D convolutions are selected by the kernel shape. This entry collects those options.
tools.usage:
ConvolutionLayer[n, {kh, kw}, "Stride" -> 2, "PaddingSize" -> 1]
ConvolutionLayer[n, 3, "PaddingSize" -> "Same"]
ConvolutionLayer[n, 3, "Dilation" -> 2]
ConvolutionLayer[n, 3, "ChannelGroups" -> n] (* depthwise *)
ConvolutionLayer[n, {3, 3, 3}] (* 3D *)
PoolingLayer[2, "Stride" -> 2, "Function" -> Mean]
tools.example: mobileBlock = NetChain[{ConvolutionLayer[32, 3, "PaddingSize" -> 1, "ChannelGroups" -> 32], BatchNormalizationLayer[], Ramp, ConvolutionLayer[64, 1], BatchNormalizationLayer[], Ramp}, "Input" -> {32, 56, 56}]

tools.name: NetInsert
tools.description: Net editing functions: NetInsert inserts a layer at a position in a NetChain, NetDelete removes layers, NetAppend/NetPrepend add layers at the ends, NetJoin concatenates chains and NetRename renames layers/ports; NetReplace replaces layers matching a pattern throughout a net (e.g. swap all Ramp for GELU) and NetReplacePart (listed) replaces by position. They allow transfer learning by modifying pretrained NetModel nets.
tools.usage:
NetInsert[chain, layer, pos]
NetDelete[chain, pos]
NetDelete[chain, {pos1, pos2}]
NetAppend[chain, layer]
NetAppend[chain, {layer1, layer2}]
NetPrepend[chain, layer]
NetJoin[chain1, chain2]
NetRename[net, {"old" -> "new"}]
NetReplace[net, _ElementwiseLayer -> ElementwiseLayer["GELU"]]
NetReplace[net, {"name" -> newLayer}]

tools.name: NetUnfold
tools.description: Produces the elementary (single-step) net of a recurrent layer or folded net, exposing its state ports so that step-by-step evaluation, custom decoding loops and stateful inference are possible; NetStateObject wraps a net to carry recurrent state between successive evaluations (streaming inference), and NetFoldOperator (listed) folds a step net over a sequence. Use these for autoregressive generation and online processing.
tools.usage:
NetUnfold[net]
step = NetUnfold[LongShortTermMemoryLayer[32]]
state = NetStateObject[net]
state[input1]; state[input2] (* state carried over *)
NetStateObject[net, initialStates]

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: Recurrent layer or net containing recurrent layers.

tools.name: NetSharedArray
tools.description: Marks an array parameter as shared between several layers (weight tying, e.g. input and output embeddings of a language model, or Siamese branches) so that they are trained as one; NetInsertSharedArrays converts all arrays of a net into shared arrays with a prefix (making copies of that net share weights when reused in a NetGraph). Shared arrays are listed by NetInformation[net, "SharedArraysList"].
tools.usage:
NetSharedArray["name"]
LinearLayer[n, "Weights" -> NetSharedArray["W"]]
EmbeddingLayer[d, "Weights" -> NetSharedArray["emb"]]
NetInsertSharedArrays[net]
NetInsertSharedArrays[net, "prefix"]
NetInformation[net, "SharedArraysList"]
tools.example:
branch = NetInsertSharedArrays[NetChain[{LinearLayer[64], Tanh, LinearLayer[16]}], "tower"];
siamese = NetGraph[<|"a" -> branch, "b" -> branch, "dist" -> ThreadingLayer[Total[(#1 - #2)^2] &]|>, {NetPort["x"] -> "a", NetPort["y"] -> "b", {"a", "b"} -> "dist"}]

tools.name: NetPortGradient
tools.description: NetPortGradient["port"] used as a property in net evaluation returns the gradient of the output with respect to an input port or parameter (saliency maps, adversarial examples, custom training loops); NetEvaluationMode -> "Train" evaluates a net in training mode (dropout active, batch statistics from the batch) versus "Test" (default). NetMeasurements (listed) computes metrics on datasets.
tools.usage:
net[input, NetPortGradient["Input"]]
net[input, NetPortGradient[{"layer", "Weights"}]]
net[input, NetEvaluationMode -> "Train"]
net[input, {"Output", NetPortGradient["Input"]}]

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Input port name or {layer, parameter} specification.

tools.name: NetEncoder Image
tools.description: NetEncoder[{"Image", size, colorspace}] converts images (files, URLs or Image objects) to arrays of a fixed size with options "MeanImage"/"VarianceImage" normalization, "Interleaving" and "ColorChannels"; "Image3D" handles volumes and "VideoFrames" samples frames from videos. It is the input encoder of every image classifier and is attached via the "Input" port of NetChain/NetGraph.
tools.usage:
NetEncoder[{"Image", {224, 224}, "RGB"}]
NetEncoder[{"Image", 32, "Grayscale"}]
NetEncoder[{"Image", {224, 224}, "ColorSpace" -> "RGB", "MeanImage" -> {0.485, 0.456, 0.406}, "VarianceImage" -> {0.229, 0.224, 0.225}^2}]
NetEncoder[{"Image3D", {32, 32, 32}}]
NetEncoder[{"VideoFrames", n}]

tools.name: NetEncoder Class
tools.description: NetEncoder[{"Class", classes}] maps class labels to integer indices (or "UnitVector" one-hot form) for classification targets, "Boolean" maps True/False to 0/1 and "Scalar" encodes numbers (with optional range scaling); the matching NetDecoder[{"Class", classes}] returns the most probable class or, with a property ("Probabilities", "TopProbabilities", "Entropy", "Decision"), the full distribution. These are the standard target encoders and output decoders of classifiers and regressors.
tools.usage:
NetEncoder[{"Class", {"a", "b", "c"}}]
NetEncoder[{"Class", classes, "UnitVector"}]
NetEncoder["Boolean"]
NetEncoder["Scalar"]
NetDecoder[{"Class", classes}]
NetDecoder[{"Class", classes, "InputDepth" -> 2}] (* per-token classes *)
NetDecoder["Boolean"]
NetDecoder["Scalar"]
net[input, "TopProbabilities" -> 3]
tools.example:
net = NetTrain[NetChain[{LinearLayer[16], Ramp, LinearLayer[3], SoftmaxLayer[]}, "Input" -> 4, "Output" -> NetDecoder[{"Class", {"setosa", "versicolor", "virginica"}}]], irisData];
net[{5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2}, "Probabilities"]

tools.name: NetEncoder Tokens
tools.description: Text encoders: NetEncoder[{"Tokens", vocab}] splits text into word tokens and maps them to indices (with "IgnoreCase", "TargetLength"), "Characters" encodes character sequences ("UnitVector" or "Index" forms), "UTF8" encodes raw bytes, "SubwordTokens" applies BPE/SentencePiece vocabularies used by transformer NetModels, and "BioSequence"-style encoders exist via "Characters" with custom alphabets; NetDecoder[{"Characters", ...}] and NetDecoder["Tokens"] decode back and "CTCBeamSearch" decodes CTC outputs.
tools.usage:
NetEncoder[{"Tokens"}] (* built-in English vocabulary *)
NetEncoder[{"Tokens", vocabList, "IgnoreCase" -> True}]
NetEncoder[{"Characters", Alphabet[], "UnitVector"}]
NetEncoder[{"Characters", chars, "TargetLength" -> 100}]
NetEncoder["UTF8"]
NetEncoder[{"SubwordTokens", vocabFile}]
NetDecoder[{"Characters", chars}]
NetDecoder[{"CTCBeamSearch", chars}]

parameters.name: vocab
parameters.description: List of tokens or characters; unknown tokens map to an extra index.

parameters.name: TargetLength
parameters.description: Pad/truncate sequences to a fixed length.

tools.name: NetEncoder Audio
tools.description: Audio encoders: "Audio" produces raw sample arrays (with "SampleRate", "TargetLength"), "AudioSpectrogram", "AudioSTFT", "AudioMelSpectrogram" and "AudioMFCC" produce time-frequency feature sequences (window size, offset, number of filters) - the inputs of speech and sound classification nets such as those in the Neural Net Repository; "FeatureExtractor" wraps any FeatureExtraction method and "Function" applies a custom function with a declared output shape.
tools.usage:
NetEncoder[{"Audio", "SampleRate" -> 16000, "TargetLength" -> 16000}]
NetEncoder[{"AudioMelSpectrogram", "NumberOfFilters" -> 64, "WindowSize" -> 1024, "Offset" -> 512}]
NetEncoder[{"AudioMFCC", "NumberOfCoefficients" -> 13}]
NetEncoder[{"AudioSTFT"}]
NetEncoder[{"FeatureExtractor", "ImageFeatures"}]
NetEncoder[{"Function", f, {n}}]

tools.name: NetDecoder Image
tools.description: NetDecoder["Image"] (and "Image3D") converts output arrays back to Image objects (with "ColorSpace" and range options) for autoencoders, generators and image-to-image nets; NetDecoder[{"Function", f}] applies a custom function to the output array, and NetDecoder["Boolean"]/"Scalar" return numbers. Decoders are attached with "Output" -> ... and can be overridden per evaluation with net[input, None] to get the raw array.
tools.usage:
NetDecoder["Image"]
NetDecoder[{"Image", "ColorSpace" -> "Grayscale"}]
NetDecoder["Image3D"]
NetDecoder[{"Function", f}]
net[input, None] (* raw array *)
net[input, "Output" -> None]

tools.name: BatchSize
tools.description: NetTrain option setting the number of examples per gradient step (Automatic chooses by memory; larger batches train faster per epoch but generalise differently); also an option of net evaluation and NetMeasurements for throughput on GPUs. MaxTrainingRounds (epochs, or a time via Quantity) and TimeGoal bound the training length, and TrainingUpdateSchedule selects which parts of the net are updated in each round.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, BatchSize -> 64]
NetTrain[net, data, MaxTrainingRounds -> 30]
NetTrain[net, data, MaxTrainingRounds -> Quantity[10, "Minutes"]]
NetTrain[net, data, TimeGoal -> 600]
net[inputs, BatchSize -> 256]
tools.example: NetTrain[net, trainData, BatchSize -> 128, MaxTrainingRounds -> 20, ValidationSet -> Scaled[0.1]]

tools.name: LearningRate
tools.description: Sub-option of the NetTrain Method ("ADAM", "SGD", "RMSProp", "SignSGD", ...) giving the initial learning rate, with "LearningRateSchedule" for decay and "L2Regularization"/"GradientClipping" as further sub-options; LearningRateMultipliers scales (or freezes with 0) the learning rate of individual layers or parameters - the key option for transfer learning (fine-tune the head, freeze the backbone).
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, Method -> {"ADAM", "LearningRate" -> 0.001}]
NetTrain[net, data, Method -> {"SGD", "LearningRate" -> 0.01, "Momentum" -> 0.9, "LearningRateSchedule" -> (0.1^Floor[#Round/10] &)}]
NetTrain[net, data, Method -> {"ADAM", "L2Regularization" -> 10^-4, "GradientClipping" -> 1}]
NetTrain[net, data, LearningRateMultipliers -> {"backbone" -> 0, "head" -> 1}]
NetTrain[net, data, LearningRateMultipliers -> {-1 -> 1, _ -> 0.1}]
tools.example: NetTrain[new, data, Method -> {"ADAM", "LearningRate" -> 3*^-4}, LearningRateMultipliers -> {"features" -> 0, _ -> 1}, MaxTrainingRounds -> 5]

tools.name: LossFunction
tools.description: NetTrain option choosing the loss: Automatic (cross-entropy for Class outputs, mean-squared for numeric), a loss layer (MeanAbsoluteLossLayer, CrossEntropyLossLayer["Index"], ContrastiveLossLayer, CTCLossLayer), a custom NetGraph with a "Loss" port, rules "port" -> loss for multi-output nets, or a weighted list. RandomSeeding controls initialisation and shuffling reproducibility.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> MeanAbsoluteLossLayer[]]
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> CrossEntropyLossLayer["Probabilities"]]
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> {"out1" -> MeanSquaredLossLayer[], "out2" -> Scaled[0.5]}]
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> lossGraph]
NetTrain[net, data, RandomSeeding -> 1234]
tools.example:
huber = FunctionLayer[Function[{y, t}, Mean[If[Abs[y - t] < 1, (y - t)^2/2, Abs[y - t] - 1/2]]]];
NetTrain[net, data, LossFunction -> NetGraph[<|"loss" -> huber|>, {{NetPort["Input"], NetPort["Target"]} -> "loss" -> NetPort["Loss"]}]]

tools.name: ValidationSet
tools.description: NetTrain option supplying held-out data (explicit examples, or Scaled[f] to split off a fraction, with "Interval" for evaluation frequency) used to track validation loss/accuracy and to select the best net ("TrainedNet" defaults to the lowest validation loss); TrainingStoppingCriterion stops early when a measurement stops improving ("Criterion" -> "Loss"/"ErrorRate", "Patience" -> n, "AbsoluteChange"/"RelativeChange").
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, ValidationSet -> Scaled[0.2]]
NetTrain[net, data, ValidationSet -> valData]
NetTrain[net, data, ValidationSet -> {valData, "Interval" -> Quantity[30, "Seconds"]}]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingStoppingCriterion -> <|"Criterion" -> "Loss", "Patience" -> 5|>]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingStoppingCriterion -> <|"Criterion" -> "ErrorRate", "AbsoluteChange" -> 0.001, "Patience" -> 3|>]

tools.name: TrainingProgressCheckpointing
tools.description: NetTrain option saving copies of the net during training ({"File", path} or {"Directory", dir} with "Interval" in rounds or time) so that long runs can be resumed or the best intermediate net recovered; NetTrain[net, data, ..., "TrainedNet"|All] and NetTrainResultsObject (listed) give access to the final and best nets, loss histories and checkpoints.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressCheckpointing -> {"Directory", "ckpt", "Interval" -> 1}]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressCheckpointing -> {"File", "latest.wlnet", "Interval" -> Quantity[10, "Minutes"]}]
NetTrain[Import["ckpt/round-5.wlnet"], data, ...] (* resume *)
tools.example: NetTrain[net, data, MaxTrainingRounds -> 50, TrainingProgressCheckpointing -> {"Directory", FileNameJoin[{$HomeDirectory, "ckpt"}], "Interval" -> 5}]

tools.name: TrainingProgressReporting
tools.description: NetTrain option controlling progress display: "Panel" (interactive, default in notebooks), "Print" (text lines for scripts/logs), "ProgressIndicator", None, or a function receiving the progress association; TrainingProgressFunction runs a callback every round/batch/time interval (logging, custom early stopping via "StopTraining"), and TrainingProgressMeasurements requests extra metrics ("Accuracy", "F1Score", "ConfusionMatrix", ...) computed during training.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressReporting -> "Print"]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressReporting -> None]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressFunction -> {Function[Print[#Round, " ", #RoundLoss]], "Interval" -> 1}]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressMeasurements -> {"Accuracy", "F1Score"}]
NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressFunction -> (If[#RoundLoss < 0.01, "StopTraining"] &)]
tools.example: NetTrain[net, data, TrainingProgressReporting -> "Print", TrainingProgressMeasurements -> {"Accuracy", "ConfusionMatrix"}, ValidationSet -> Scaled[0.1]]

tools.name: TargetDevice
tools.description: Option of NetTrain, net evaluation, NetMeasurements and NetModel choosing "CPU" (default) or "GPU" (NVIDIA CUDA; {"GPU", n} selects a device) for computation; WorkingPrecision -> "Real32" (default), "Real64" or "Mixed" sets numeric precision. GPU training requires the CUDA paclet resources, downloaded automatically on first use.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data, TargetDevice -> "GPU"]
NetTrain[net, data, TargetDevice -> {"GPU", 2}]
net[inputs, TargetDevice -> "GPU"]
NetTrain[net, data, WorkingPrecision -> "Mixed"]
tools.example:
res = NetTrain[net, data, TargetDevice -> "GPU", BatchSize -> 256, MaxTrainingRounds -> 10];
res["TotalTrainingTime"]

tools.name: NetTrainResultsObject properties
tools.description: NetTrain[net, data, All] returns a NetTrainResultsObject (listed) with properties "TrainedNet", "FinalNet", "LossEvolutionPlot", "RoundLossList", "ValidationLossList", "ValidationMeasurementsLists", "TotalTrainingTime", "BatchesPerRound", "CheckpointingFiles", "BestValidationRound", "ExamplesProcessed"; NetTrain[net, data, "prop"] returns just one. NetMeasurements[net, testData, {"Accuracy", "ConfusionMatrixPlot", "ROCCurvePlot"}] evaluates a trained net on held-out data.
tools.usage:
res = NetTrain[net, data, All]
res["TrainedNet"]
res["LossEvolutionPlot"]
res["ValidationLossList"]
NetTrain[net, data, "RoundLossList"]
NetMeasurements[res["TrainedNet"], test, {"Accuracy", "F1Score", "ConfusionMatrixPlot"}]
tools.example:
res = NetTrain[net, train, All, ValidationSet -> Scaled[0.2], MaxTrainingRounds -> 30];
res["LossEvolutionPlot"]
NetMeasurements[res["TrainedNet"], test, "ConfusionMatrixPlot"]
Export["model.wlnet", res["TrainedNet"]]

tools.name: NetModel repository usage
tools.description: NetModel (listed) fetches pretrained nets from the Wolfram Neural Net Repository by name, with parameter variants NetModel[{"name", "Size" -> "Large"}], property arguments ("Properties", "ByteArrays"-free "UninitializedEvaluationNet", "EvaluationNet", "TrainingNet", "ParametersInformation", "ExampleInput"), and "NetModel Import" of ONNX/PyTorch/MXNet models via Import["model.onnx"]. Combine with NetTake/NetDrop for feature extraction and NetReplacePart for new heads.
tools.usage:
NetModel["ResNet-50 Trained on ImageNet Competition Data"]
NetModel[{"BERT Trained on BookCorpus and English Wikipedia Data", "Type" -> "Base", "InputType" -> "ListOfStrings"}]
NetModel["name", "ParametersInformation"]
NetModel["name", "UninitializedEvaluationNet"]
Import["model.onnx"]
Export["model.onnx", net]
